newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin leaves hospital, faces political scandal.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin leaves hospital, faces political scandal.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin left hospital on Friday to continue his recovery from heart surgery in a government rest home, but immediately faced pressure from parliament to remove his powerful chief-of staff.
The State Duma lower chamber urged Yeltsin to drop Anatoly Chubais until he has investigated allegations of irregularities in the funding of his re-election campaign this summer.
Chubais, loathed by the opposition communists who dominate the Duma, denied any wrongdoing and told Interfax news agency he was ready to help state prosecutors investigate.
"I am ready to answer all questions," he said.
The scandal is the latest to undermine Yeltsin's authority during his almost constant absence from the Kremlin since he fell ill just before the second round of voting on July 3.
The 65-year-old president received Chubais at the government sanatorium at Barvikha, just outside Moscow, after checking out of the capital's Central Clinical Hospital earlier on Friday.
It was not clear if they had discussed the Duma appeal during their 50-minute conversation, Yeltsin's second official meeting since his quintuple bypass operation on November 5.

Sergei Mironov, the chief Kremlin doctor, said Yeltsin was now able to work up to six hours a day. He told reporters the convalescence period was due to end on December 20 but that Yeltsin would be able to visit the Kremlin before then.
Yeltsin, wearing a fur hat and long dark coat, had waved cheerfully as he stepped into a limousine for the short drive to Barvikha, where he will spent the next two or three weeks.
"The president was clearly in a good mood when he left," Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said.
"The president's blood pressure is normal and his pulse averages 80," he told a news briefing, quoting doctors who examined Yeltsin just before he left the hospital.
Underlining Yeltsin's ability to work, Yastrzhembsky said the president had played an important role in Russian mediation which helped defuse a politicial crisis in neighbouring Belarus.

Yeltsin spoke by telephone with Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko and parliament chairman Semyon Sharetsky earlier this week. The rivals reached a compromise on Friday in their dispute over a planned referendum on extending Lukashenko's powers.

But Yeltsin faced a difficult problem over the political scandal, although he appeared likely to ignore the Duma's appeal to temporarily remove Chubais and first deputy prime minister Viktor Ilyushin, a former Kremlin aide.

Chubais, a 41-year-old former privatisation guru, masterminded Yeltsin's re-election and is the main strategy maker in the Kremlin. The communists say he has unconstitutionally amassed power during the president's absence.
The Duma's non-binding appeal was adopted by 263 votes for and none against. One deputy abstained and the other members of the 450-seat house did not attend.

State prosecutors plan to investigate the scandal, which erupted last week when the Moskovsky Komsomolets newspaper published a transcript of what it said was a bugged conversation between Ilyushin, Chubais and another official on June 22.

The transcript portrayed Chubais and Ilyushin as conspiring to block an investigation by prosecutors into the detention of two of their campaign staff, allegedly caught leaving the government building with half a million dollars in cash.
At the time all those involved in the incident, which took place between the two rounds of the election, denied the two men were carrying the money and said they were framed.
